A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Horizon Reduction Makes RL Scalable. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G support reliable comparison; relocated figures and renumbered references and tables were matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original OGBench scaling experiments, combination-lock experiments, and algorithm and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds reward-based single-task evaluations, batch-size experiments, and additional ablation curves.

M1.justification: SHARSA and double SHARSA retain their hierarchical flow policies, SARSA objectives, and rejection-sampling procedures in Section 6.2 and Appendix E.3. The IQL-based SHARSA variant used in the added evaluations already appeared in v1's Appendix C.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds reward-based, non-goal-conditioned task1 evaluations for cube-quadruple, puzzle-4x5, puzzle-4x6, and humanoidmaze-giant. These extend task requirements within the existing simulated domains; the original goal-conditioned benchmarks and combination-lock coverage remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a standalone SARSA comparator. Figure 12 adds IQL value-learning variants with kappa 0.7 and 0.9 to the puzzle-4x6 panel, which showed only SARSA in v1. The main scaling experiments retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The new single-task comparison uses 100M transitions for cube and 1B for the other tasks, reports performance at the 1M epoch, and uses AWR with alpha 10 for SARSA and IQL. Figure 11 adds batch sizes 2048 and 4096 against the 1024 default. Existing evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a sensitivity test asking whether larger batches overcome poor scaling, expanding Figure 11 from eight to nine analyses. Figure 12 also completes the puzzle-4x6 value-learning ablation with two IQL variants. The other ablation questions are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four random seeds unless otherwise noted, 95% confidence bands, and standard deviations in the full result tables. Added uncertainty entries and small changes to existing confidence-band values do not introduce a different reporting practice or establish increased run counts.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds single-task results: on humanoidmaze-giant, n-SAC+BC reports 88±3, SHARSA with kappa 0.5 reports 26±4, and its kappa 0.7 variant reports 87±3. Figures 11–12 add batch-size and IQL curves and update some confidence-band values. These are additions under specified settings; v1 Tables 4–5 retain their values as v3 Tables 5–6.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and equations (1)–(32) are unchanged, with no added theorem, proof, or derivation. The new footnote explaining effective decision horizon clarifies terminology already used in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: standard offline RL scales poorly on difficult tasks, horizon reduction improves scalability, and SHARSA provides a simple implementation. The added experiments supply support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D explicitly discuss applicability beyond goal-conditioned benchmarks. Appendix D explains that absent hindsight relabeling increases suboptimality and can make IQL-based value learning useful for SHARSA. Section 7 retains the existing limitations concerning hierarchy depth, short-segment optimality, and nonmonotonic scaling.

D1.justification: Appendix D documents the added tasks' identifiers, dataset sizes, evaluation checkpoint, IQL expectile, AWR coefficient, and SAC+BC regularization coefficients of 0.01 for humanoidmaze and 0.1 otherwise. Figure 11 identifies the added batch sizes. Existing implementation descriptions, hardware information, and code/data access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Imani and White's 2018 paper on distributional losses to the HL-Gauss discussion, replacing v1's duplicated citation. Appendix B additionally cites the already-listed ReBRAC work to support the baseline choice. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds a terminology footnote, a scope clarification in Section 3, and short explanatory passages in Appendices B and D. Appendix cross-references change to section terminology, and the publication footer changes to NeurIPS 2025. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 1, expands Figure 11 with a batch-size row, and adds two curves to Figure 12 while moving it from page 20 to page 21. Nearby text and figures reflow, and subsequent tables are renumbered. The remaining visual organization is largely retained.

improvement.justification: The reward-based results strengthen evidence for applicability beyond the original goal-conditioned OGBench evaluation. The batch-size control and completed IQL ablation also address specific gaps in empirical support. These gains are bounded: the new task comparison reports one checkpoint within existing simulated domains, while the main method, scaling results, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
